title: The Saturday Hour and the Blind Dictation: Basel, the Neva, Berlin, and the Neva Again
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Basel, birth in the pastor's house
stops.date_confidence: attested; MacTutor and Wikipedia agree on 15 April 1707
stops.campa: On the fifteenth of April a son is born in Basel to Paul Euler, a Reformed pastor, and to Marguerite Brucker. They name him Leonhard. The Confederacy is small and its learned houses fewer still, and the one he is born into already holds the two disciplines that will contend for him: the Calvinism of the pulpit, and the mathematics of the Bernoullis, who teach in this town. No source reached this session fixes the street of the house or the church of the baptism, and this pin marks the old town rather than a doorway. Basel keeps the date and has lost the address.
suggested_refs: Baptismal registers of the Basel Reformed parishes, 1707, for the unlocated birth house

stops.name: Riehen, the village parsonage
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: Paul Euler takes the Reformed pastorate of Riehen, a village of vines and orchards an hour outside the city walls, and the family moves there while Leonhard is still an infant. He spends most of his childhood in the parsonage. The village has a church, a school for letters and psalms, and nothing past that; whatever mathematics the boy meets before he is eight he meets at home or not at all. Basel is visible from the ridge above the village, close enough to walk to and far enough that a child has to be sent.
suggested_refs: The Dorfkirche of Riehen and the parsonage of Paul Euler

stops.name: University of Basel, matriculation at thirteen
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown. Sources give his age at matriculation as thirteen or fourteen
stops.campa: At about eight he is sent into Basel to lodge with his maternal grandmother and attend the Latin school, Riehen having no schooling past the elementary; that arrangement is traditional rather than documented, and the house is not identified. At thirteen he matriculates at the university for the general arts course, his father intending the ministry. Carl Jung will matriculate in this same university and Friedrich Nietzsche will hold its chair of classical philology, both of them a century and a half downstream of this enrolment.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the University of Basel, 1720

stops.name: Basel, the Saturday hour with Johann Bernoulli
stops.date_confidence: the tutelage is attested for 1720-1723; this stop is placed in its first full year, with no month or day recorded
stops.campa: Johann Bernoulli, the foremost mathematician in Europe and a man who does not give lessons, agrees to see the boy at his own house on Saturday afternoons. Euler reads the hard books alone through the week and brings his difficulties to the table. The exact address of the Bernoulli residence is not established here and this pin is a placement in the old town. Two centuries later Hermann Hesse marries Maria Bernoulli, whom the corpus records as being of the Basel family of mathematicians. The family is this one.
suggested_refs: The Bernoulli residence in old Basel, address unestablished

stops.name: University of Basel, the Master's degree: Descartes against Newton
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: He takes the Master of Philosophy with a dissertation setting the natural philosophy of Descartes against that of Newton, who is alive in London and will die four years later. His father's plan is unaltered by the performance. Leonhard enters theology, with Hebrew and Greek, and keeps the mathematics running underneath it. That Bernoulli was eventually the one who told Paul Euler his son was a mathematician is tradition, not document. The pulpit loses the argument and keeps the habit; Euler prays every day of his life.
suggested_refs: Euler's 1723 master's dissertation comparing Descartes and Newton

stops.name: University of Basel, the dissertation on sound and the chair refused
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: He finishes at Basel with Dissertatio physica de sono, on the propagation of sound, and applies for the university's vacant professorship of physics. He is nineteen and he does not get it. The Swiss republics have few chairs and long queues, and the men ahead of him are not obviously better, only older. Daniel and Nicolaus Bernoulli have already gone east to St Petersburg, to an Academy of Sciences founded on a marsh a year or two before, and word of its vacancies comes back along the same road.
suggested_refs: Dissertatio physica de sono, Basel, 1726

stops.name: Basel, the Schifflande: leaving Switzerland for good
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; ru.wikipedia states he left Switzerland forever on 5 April 1727. The Rhine landing is the likely embarkation point rather than a documented one
stops.campa: His entry in the Paris Academy competition on the best placement of masts in a ship takes second prize, written by a man from a landlocked republic. The St Petersburg offer comes through the Bernoullis and it is a post in medicine rather than in mathematics; he takes it. On the fifth of April he boards a boat at the Rhine landing below the old town and goes down the river, then overland by post-wagon across the German states. He is twenty. He never sets foot in Switzerland again.
suggested_refs: The Schifflande, Basel, departure point for Rhine traffic downstream

stops.name: Lubeck harbour, the passage north
stops.date_confidence: month attested; day unknown, defaulted to the first
stops.campa: The post-wagons put him down at Lubeck on the Baltic, where the Hanseatic quays send timber and salt and passengers up to the Russian capital. He waits out the days for a sailing. The crossing is the last stretch of some six weeks out of Basel, and everything behind him now is the Rhine and the German roads. He does not speak the court language of the place he is going to, and nobody has warned him about the winter. The Academy that has hired him has hired him as a physician.
suggested_refs: The Lubeck Baltic packet route to St Petersburg in the 1720s

stops.name: Kunstkamera, St Petersburg: arrival at the wrong department
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; no source consulted states whether the date is Old or New Style, and Russia was on the Julian calendar
stops.campa: He lands on the seventeenth of May, and the Academy that hired him puts him in the medical division rather than in mathematics. He lodges with Daniel Bernoulli, his friend from the Basel years, and works beside him. The building is the Kunstkamera on Vasilievsky Island, the Tsar's cabinet of curiosities with an academy of sciences grafted onto it, a few years old and already short of money. Euler is twenty, and he has arrived in the city where he will spend thirty-one of the fifty-six years left to him.
suggested_refs: The Kunstkamera on Vasilievsky Island, first home of the Imperial Academy of Sciences

stops.name: St Petersburg, medical lieutenant in the Russian navy
stops.date_confidence: the service is attested for 1727 and the years following; no month or day is recorded, and this stop is placed after the arrival
stops.campa: The Academy's funding is precarious and its imported Swiss mathematicians are surplus. Euler is commissioned a medical lieutenant in the Russian navy and serves in that rank while he waits for a scientific appointment. The sources that record the service do not record where he served it; the naval base at Kronstadt is an inference and has been left out of this journey for that reason. A pastor's son from a river town keeps the sick-list of a fleet, and writes mathematics in the hours the fleet does not want.
suggested_refs: Russian navy medical service records, 1727-1730, for the unlocated posting

stops.name: Imperial Academy of Sciences, the professorship of physics
stops.date_confidence: ru.wikipedia gives 22 January 1731 and en-Wikipedia gives 1731; MacTutor gives 1730. The 1730 reading is the minority one and is not adopted here, but it is not refuted either
stops.campa: The naval interlude ends with a professorship of physics at the Academy. The Russian account is specific about the date, the twenty-second of January; the standard English biography puts the promotion a year earlier, and the two have never been reconciled. Either way the medical appointment is finished and Euler is where he was always meant to be. The Academy pays late and quarrels with itself, and it prints everything he writes. For a young man with no patrimony that is a good bargain, and he takes it for life.
suggested_refs: Protocols of the Imperial Academy of Sciences, January 1731

stops.name: Imperial Academy of Sciences, head of the mathematics division
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: Daniel Bernoulli, worn down by the climate and the politics, goes home to Basel, and Euler at twenty-six takes his place at the head of the Academy's mathematics division. He has been in Russia six years. The last of the Bernoullis has gone back up the road he himself came down, and the pupil who followed them east now holds the chair alone. The correspondence between the two men runs for decades along that road, question and objection and counter-example travelling by post between the Rhine and the Neva.
suggested_refs: The Euler-Daniel Bernoulli correspondence, Basel and St Petersburg

stops.name: St Petersburg, the house on the Neva and the marriage to Katharina Gsell
stops.date_confidence: marriage attested to the day. The house purchase is dated 1733 by ru.wikipedia, that is, before the wedding rather than after it as some accounts have it; the two events are carried on one pin here
stops.campa: He buys a house on the Neva embankment, and on the seventh of January he marries Katharina Gsell, daughter of Georg Gsell, the Swiss painter the Tsar brought to Petersburg to hang his pictures. Thirteen children will be born to them and five will live past infancy. Their first son, Johann Albrecht, arrives within the year, with Christian Goldbach standing as godfather. No source names the church of the wedding. Which house on which stretch of embankment is also unsettled, and this pin is an approximation.
stops.quote: He had by his first wife thirteen children, eight of whom died young. His three sons survived him.
stops.quote_source: Elogium of Euler, prefixed to Letters of Euler ... Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1. Long-s normalised from the archive.org scan
suggested_refs: The Euler house on the Neva embankment, Vasilievsky Island, address disputed

stops.name: Imperial Academy of Sciences, the geography department and the fever
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: He takes charge of the Academy's geography department and the mapping of the Russian Empire, a labour of surveys, star-sights and arithmetic performed on a country whose eastern edge nobody has measured. He works at it the way he works at everything, which is without pause, and a fever nearly kills him. The eulogy read after his death traces the ruin of one eye to exactly this exertion. Other accounts put the loss three or five years later and blame the maps rather than the fever, and they have not been reconciled.
stops.quote: In 1735, the exertion occasioned by an astronomical calculation ... brought on an indisposition, which issued in the loss of one of his eyes.
stops.quote_source: Elogium of Euler, prefixed to Letters of Euler ... Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1. Long-s normalised from the archive.org scan
suggested_refs: The Academy's general map of the Russian Empire, on which Euler worked from 1735
sources: Hunter, Letters of Euler (1795), vol. 1, Elogium

stops.name: Imperial Academy of Sciences, the Basel problem
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: The question is old and the mathematicians of Basel had not answered it: what exact quantity do you reach by adding the reciprocals of all the square numbers, forever. Euler reaches it. The problem is called the Basel problem after the town that both he and the men who failed at it came from, and the solution makes him, at twenty-eight, a name in every academy in Europe. He does the work in a city two thousand miles from the town it is named for, and he never sees that town again.
suggested_refs: Euler's solution of the Basel problem, St Petersburg, 1735

stops.name: Imperial Academy of Sciences, the seven bridges of Konigsberg
stops.date_confidence: presented to the Academy on 26 August 1735. The paper appeared only in 1741, in the Commentarii volume nominally covering 1736, which is why 1736 circulates as the date of the work; that year is the volume year and not the year of the solution
stops.campa: A town he has never seen, far to the west on the Pregel, has seven bridges over two branches of the river and an island in the middle, and its citizens want to know whether a walk can cross each bridge exactly once. On the twenty-sixth of August he presents the answer: it cannot, and the reason has nothing to do with distance or with the shape of the town, only with how many bridges meet at each bank. Immanuel Kant is eleven years old in that town, and will never leave it.
suggested_refs: Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis, presented 1735, printed 1741

stops.name: St Petersburg, Mechanica
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: Mechanica appears in two volumes: Newton's dynamics taken out of the geometry of the Principia and rewritten in the analytic language of the calculus, so that a problem of motion becomes a problem of equations rather than a problem of drawing. It is the form in which physics will be done from here on. Newton has been dead nine years and never saw his own system said this way. Euler is twenty-nine and has been in Russia nine years, and the Academy prints him faster than Europe can read him.
suggested_refs: Mechanica sive motus scientia analytice exposita, St Petersburg, 1736

stops.name: St Petersburg, the right eye
stops.date_confidence: 1738 per MacTutor and Wikipedia. The Hunter Elogium dates the ruin of the eye to the illness of 1735; other accounts put it around 1740 and blame the Academy's cartographic work. Three readings, none refuted
stops.campa: The sight goes out of his right eye. He blames the cartography, the years of small figures and smaller print done for the Academy's map of the Empire. The eulogy blames the fever of three years back. A third account puts the loss around 1740 and the sources have never been made to agree. No account disputes the rest. He is thirty-one and has lost half his sight, and the volume of his production does not change by a single paper. The Academy sets him to more of the same work.
suggested_refs: Contemporary accounts of Euler's first blindness, 1735-1740
sources: Hunter, Letters of Euler (1795), vol. 1, Elogium

stops.name: St Petersburg, the Neva port: departure for Berlin
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; calendar style not stated in any source consulted
stops.campa: He has taken the Paris Grand Prize twice in three years, sharing it in 1738 for the nature of fire and in 1740 for the tides. Empress Anna is dead, the regency is unstable, and foreigners in the Academy are being watched. Frederick the Great, new on the Prussian throne and rebuilding his academy, sends an invitation. On the nineteenth of June Euler leaves the city with his wife, his children and his household, after fourteen years. He does not resign his Russian pension, and he will be back.
suggested_refs: Frederick the Great's invitation to Euler, 1740-1741

stops.name: Berlin, arrival at the Academy
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: He arrives on the twenty-fifth of July, five weeks out of Petersburg. Berlin is a garrison capital with a king who writes French verse and wants an academy to match Paris, and Euler is the mathematics of it. Around this address on Unter den Linden the corpus keeps gathering. Fichte will take refuge in this quarter in 1799 and lecture the Addresses to the German Nation into it, and Gauss will lodge nearby with Humboldt. Euler is the first of them to hold the mathematical chair of Prussia.
suggested_refs: The Berlin Academy buildings on Unter den Linden, Euler's institutional home 1741-1766

stops.name: Berlin, the court and the silent geometer
stops.date_confidence: no date is attested for the exchange with the Queen Mother; the stop is placed in his first months at court, and the pin is a placement rather than a known address
stops.campa: He settles his household in the streets behind the Academy. The precise address before the Charlottenburg purchase is not established, and this pin is a placement. At court he is a disappointment. Frederick wants wit at the supper table and gets a Calvinist who answers what he is asked and volunteers nothing further. The Queen Mother presses him on the silence, and the answer she gets is repeated for two hundred years. The king keeps him for twenty-five years and never once warms to him.
stops.quote: I have just come from a country, where people are hanged, if they talk.
stops.quote_source: Elogium of Euler, prefixed to Letters of Euler ... Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1. Long-s normalised from the archive.org scan
suggested_refs: Euler's Berlin residence before 1753, address unestablished
sources: Hunter, Letters of Euler (1795), vol. 1, Elogium
Alexander Vucinich, Science in Russian Culture (1963), as a later carrier of the anecdote

stops.name: Berlin, director of the mathematics class
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: He is appointed director of the mathematical class of the Berlin Academy. The standard account has the Academy founded in this year under Maupertuis, and the standard account is wrong twice over: the Society of Sciences dates from 1700 with Leibniz as its first president, 1744 is the year the Nouvelle Societe Litteraire is merged into it, and Maupertuis does not take the presidency until 1746. The directorship itself is not in doubt, and the mathematics of Prussia is run from this desk.
suggested_refs: Prussian Academy of Sciences, foundation 1700 and merger of 1744

stops.name: Berlin, Introductio in analysin infinitorum
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: The Introductio in analysin infinitorum appears in two volumes and moves the centre of mathematics off the curve and onto the function. Before it, analysis is about geometrical objects. After it, analysis is about the rule that carries a number to a number, and the curve is only a picture of the rule. Every textbook since is downstream of that decision. He writes it in Berlin, in Latin, for an academy whose king reads French by preference and does not read this.
suggested_refs: Introductio in analysin infinitorum, Lausanne, 1748

stops.name: Sanssouci, the fountains that will not rise
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown. The Finow Canal work mentioned here rests on one biography and is not independently confirmed
stops.campa: Frederick wants water thrown into the air at Sanssouci as it is thrown at Versailles, and sets his geometer to the hydraulics. Euler computes the pipes and the pressures, the fountains do not work, and the king holds it against him for the rest of their acquaintance. The same year he is given the calculations for the Finow Canal between the Havel and the Oder, a claim that rests on a single biography. Francisco de Miranda will watch this king drill his army on this ground in 1785.
suggested_refs: The waterworks of Sanssouci and Euler's hydraulic calculations, 1749

stops.name: Charlottenburg, the house and the mother from Basel
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown. The exact plot is not identified and this pin marks the district near the palace
stops.campa: He buys a house at Charlottenburg outside the city, with garden and land enough to be called a farm, and installs the household in it: Katharina, the surviving children, and his widowed mother Marguerite Brucker, whom he has brought out of Switzerland to live with him. The plan the pastor made for his son ended long ago. The pastor's widow ends her life in the house the mathematics bought. The exact plot in Charlottenburg is not identified in any source reached, and this pin marks the district.
suggested_refs: Euler's Charlottenburg house and farm, plot unidentified

stops.name: Berlin, Institutiones calculi differentialis
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: The Institutiones calculi differentialis is published, the differential calculus set out entire and in order for the first time, in the language and the notation that will be taught for the next two centuries. The same year the Royal Swedish Academy and the French Academy of Sciences elect him a foreign member. He is forty-eight and has one eye. He is writing faster than the Berlin Academy's own printers can set him, and the backlog that will outlive him by fifty years starts here.
stops.quote: It has been said that, to men of great talents, the pleasure of exertion is a reward still more gratifying than glory itself: were it necessary to prove this truth by examples, that of Euler would put it beyond a doubt.
stops.quote_source: Elogium of Euler, prefixed to Letters of Euler ... Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1. Long-s normalised from the archive.org scan
suggested_refs: Institutiones calculi differentialis, Berlin, 1755

stops.name: Berlin, Maupertuis dead and the presidency withheld
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: Maupertuis dies and the presidency of the Academy falls vacant. Euler has effectively been directing its science for years and now does so outright, and Frederick withholds the title from him. The king wants a name with French conversation at the head of his academy; what he has is a one-eyed Swiss who works. The arrangement holds for seven years on both sides. Euler does the labour of a president and is not one, and complains of it to nobody who writes the complaint down.
suggested_refs: The vacant presidency of the Berlin Academy, 1759-1766

stops.name: Charlottenburg, the farm plundered
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown. The farm's location distinct from the house is not pinpointed in the source, so the same coordinate is reused
stops.campa: The Seven Years War reaches Brandenburg and Russian troops advancing on Berlin sack the farm at Charlottenburg. When General Saltykov learns whose property it was he orders compensation, and Empress Elizabeth in Petersburg adds four thousand rubles on top of that, an unusual courtesy from an enemy power to a man who left her Academy nineteen years earlier. The same Empress's armies are at that moment sitting in Konigsberg, whose bridges he solved without ever going there.
suggested_refs: Russian compensation to Euler for the sack of his Charlottenburg farm, 1760

stops.name: Charlottenburg, the Letters to a German Princess
stops.date_confidence: written 1760-1762; the stop is dated to the first year of writing. Publication is later: volumes one and two at St Petersburg in 1768 and volume three at Frankfurt in 1774
stops.campa: Between 1760 and 1762 he writes two hundred and thirty-four letters on natural philosophy to Friederike Charlotte of Brandenburg-Schwedt and her younger sister Louise: light, sound, gravity, magnetism, logic and the soul, in French, without a single equation. They are the most widely read thing he ever writes. The first two volumes appear at St Petersburg in 1768 and the third at Frankfurt in 1774, by which time he has left Berlin for good and cannot see the pages.
stops.quote: For the instruction of a young and sensible female.
stops.quote_source: Translator's Preface, Letters of Euler on Different Subjects in Physics and Philosophy, Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1
suggested_refs: Lettres a une princesse d'Allemagne, 234 letters, 1760-1762
sources: Hunter, Letters of Euler (1795), vol. 1, Translator's Preface

stops.name: Berlin, d'Alembert declines and Russia writes
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: Frederick offers the presidency of the Academy to d'Alembert in Paris. D'Alembert refuses it, Frederick appoints nobody, and the slight is now a matter of record in front of the whole learned world. Euler, fifty-six, passed over four years running in an academy he has been running, opens a correspondence with St Petersburg, where Catherine has taken the Russian throne and is rebuilding the institution he walked out of. The negotiation runs three years and neither king nor empress hurries it.
suggested_refs: Frederick the Great's offer of the Berlin presidency to d'Alembert, 1763

stops.name: Berlin, the leave granted
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: Catherine the Great offers terms no academy in Europe will match: a salary beyond anything Berlin pays him, a pension settled on his wife, appointments for his sons, and the direction of the Academy in everything but the name. Frederick refuses permission to leave, refuses again, then grants it, and is reported furious afterwards. Euler goes out of Prussia after twenty-five years with his household and his manuscripts. He is fifty-nine and he is about to go blind.
suggested_refs: Catherine the Great's terms for Euler's return, 1766

segments.name: The Second Petersburg and the Dark

stops.name: Kunstkamera, St Petersburg: the return under Catherine
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: He comes back to the Neva after twenty-five years, received as the greatest ornament an empress can buy, and resumes his place at the Academy. His son Johann Albrecht, born in the house on the embankment in 1734, is given a chair of physics in the same institution. Francisco de Miranda will be presented to this same empress at Kiev twenty-one years from now and taken into her favour. In 1766 Euler is the article of prestige she is buying, and she knows exactly what she has bought.
suggested_refs: Catherine the Great's re-founded Imperial Academy of Sciences, 1766

stops.name: St Petersburg, the second eye
stops.date_confidence: the illness and the discovery of the cataract are dated 1766. The couching operation is dated 1766 by en-Wikipedia, which has it performed weeks after the discovery, and 1771 by MacTutor. Both readings are carried in this journey and neither is resolved
stops.campa: Weeks after his return an illness takes most of what is left of his sight, and a cataract is found in the good eye. The sources split here and have not been made to agree. The English account has the couching done at once, in this year, with a few days of restored vision and then infection and dark; the standard biography puts the operation five years later. Both agree that from about this time Leonhard Euler cannot see, and that it makes no measurable difference to how much he produces.
suggested_refs: Contemporary accounts of Euler's cataract and its couching, 1766 and 1771

stops.name: St Petersburg, the house at evening prayer
stops.date_confidence: no date is attested for this practice. The source dates it only by his eyesight, which bounds it before the final blindness; the stop is placed between the 1766 return and the 1771 operation
stops.campa: The household is large: sons, grandchildren, servants, and the pupils who lodge under the roof. Every evening while his sight lasts he gathers them all and reads the devotion himself, keeping with what the eulogy calls scrupulous exactness the rigid Calvinism of his country. He publishes a demonstration of the existence of God and of the spirituality of the soul. The pastor's son did not become a pastor and never stopped being a pastor's son. The source dates this scene only by his eyes.
stops.quote: As long as his sight remained, he every evening collected, to domestic devotion, his grand-children, his domestics, and such of his pupils as lodged in the house.
stops.quote_source: Elogium of Euler, prefixed to Letters of Euler ... Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1. Long-s normalised from the archive.org scan
suggested_refs: Euler's Rettung der gottlichen Offenbarung and his defence of the spirituality of the soul
sources: Hunter, Letters of Euler (1795), vol. 1, Elogium

stops.name: St Petersburg, the fire and the couching
stops.date_confidence: the fire is attested to 1771; month and day unknown. The couching operation is dated 1771 by MacTutor and 1766 by en-Wikipedia, and the conflict is unresolved
stops.campa: Fire takes the house on the embankment and the blind man is carried out of it. In the same year a surgeon couches the cataract; for a few days he reads again, then the eye inflames and closes for good. He is sixty-four. A slate and chalk in characters large enough to feel his way across are what remains to him of reading, and everything else he dictates to whoever is in the room. The books and the papers have to be replaced or else remembered, and he remembers them.
stops.quote: He preserved still the faculty of distinguishing large characters traced on a slate with chalk.
stops.quote_source: Elogium of Euler, prefixed to Letters of Euler ... Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1. Long-s normalised from the archive.org scan
suggested_refs: The 1771 fire on the Neva embankment and the rescue of Euler
sources: Hunter, Letters of Euler (1795), vol. 1, Elogium

stops.name: St Petersburg, Katharina dies and Fuss arrives
stops.date_confidence: both events are attested to 1773; months and days unknown. Some accounts date Fuss's arrival to 1772, but Wikipedia's article on him gives 1773 and his assistantship as 1773-1783
stops.campa: Katharina Gsell dies, after thirty-nine years of marriage and thirteen births. In the same year a young Swiss named Nicolas Fuss arrives to work as his mathematical assistant, and stays ten years, to the end. Fuss will marry Albertine Euler, the granddaughter, and become the family's second mathematician. The line that began with Johann Bernoulli's Saturday afternoons comes back to the Neva in the person of a boy from the same small country, to be the eyes of the man it started with.
suggested_refs: Nicolas Fuss, mathematical assistant to Euler 1773-1783 and later his grandson-in-law

stops.name: St Petersburg, a paper a week
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the figure is an average for the year and not a count of dated papers
stops.campa: Blind nine years, he is producing on average one mathematical paper a week. He holds the work in his head entire and dictates it out. The eulogy records two of his pupils summing a complicated convergent series as far as the seventeenth term and disagreeing at the fiftieth figure, the difference settled by Euler doing the whole calculation in his head. He is sixty-eight. The Academy cannot print him as fast as he can speak, and the backlog begins that will take it fifty years to clear.
stops.quote: At length his facility of calculation by the head was carried to such a degree as would exceed all belief, had not the history of his labours accustomed us to prodigies.
stops.quote_source: Elogium of Euler, prefixed to Letters of Euler ... Addressed to a German Princess, trans. Henry Hunter (London, 1795), vol. 1. Long-s normalised from the archive.org scan
suggested_refs: The dictated papers of Euler's blind period, 1771-1783
sources: Hunter, Letters of Euler (1795), vol. 1, Elogium

stops.name: St Petersburg, the second marriage
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: He marries Salome Abigail Gsell, half-sister of Katharina, and the marriage lasts until his death seven years later. He is sixty-nine and he cannot see her. The household goes on as before, the same family and the same name, the widowed geometer keeping the Gsell connection that the painter's daughter brought him in 1734. What the second marriage was for, no source consulted says. That it happened is the whole of what is recorded, and the record is not embarrassed by it.

stops.name: St Petersburg, the eighteenth of September
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; MacTutor gives the haemorrhage at about five in the afternoon and death at about eleven at night. Calendar style not stated in any source consulted
stops.campa: He spends the day as he spends every day, and in the afternoon he is talking with Anders Johan Lexell about the orbit of Uranus, discovered two years earlier and not yet fitted to a curve. He says that he is dying. A haemorrhage in the brain takes him some hours later, at seventy-six. Condorcet's eulogy adds a grandchild's lesson and balloon calculations chalked that morning on two boards; those details come from the eulogy and not from anything behind it that could be reached.

segments.name: The Grave, the Edition, and the Legend

stops.name: Smolensk Lutheran Cemetery, the grave beside Katharina
stops.date_confidence: the burial date is not attested in any source reached; the stop is placed the day after the death
stops.campa: He is buried on Vasilievsky Island in the Lutheran ground of the Smolensk cemeteries, beside Katharina, in the German and Swiss quarter of the dead that the imperial capital keeps for its imported specialists. The Orthodox cemetery adjoins it; Taras Shevchenko will lie in that ground briefly in 1861 before Ukraine takes him home. The Academy goes on printing Euler's unpublished manuscripts for nearly fifty years after the funeral. Three different coordinates circulate for this plot.
suggested_refs: The Smolensk Lutheran Cemetery, Vasilievsky Island, plot coordinates disputed

stops.name: Smolensk Lutheran Cemetery, the Academy's new stone
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown
stops.campa: Fifty-four years after the funeral the Russian Academy of Sciences replaces the marker over the grave, which has deteriorated, with a new monument. What happened to the plot in the interval is recorded nowhere that could be reached, and the gap is stated here as a gap. The Academy that could not print him fast enough while he lived is still, in 1837, publishing him for the first time out of a backlog it has not exhausted. Two generations of Russian mathematicians have now been taught out of papers written by a blind man in this city, and the man is still producing.
suggested_refs: The 1837 monument raised by the Russian Academy of Sciences over Euler's grave

stops.name: Basel, the Euler Commission and the Opera Omnia
stops.date_confidence: the sources say only 'early twentieth century' for the start of the critical edition; 1907 is a representative year inside that span and is not itself attested
stops.campa: The town he left at twenty and never came back to takes charge of the collected works. The Euler Commission of the Swiss Academy of Sciences begins the Opera Omnia and has not finished it. Gustaf Enestrom's catalogue, completed in 1913, counts eight hundred and sixty-six distinct publications, about four fifths of them in Latin. The Kunstmuseum a few streets away holds Jakob Emanuel Handmann's pastel of 1753, the face people mean when they mean Euler. Paracelsus burned Avicenna in this town. It prints Euler.

stops.name: Lazarevskoe Cemetery, the remains moved
stops.date_confidence: the year is contested three ways: Wikipedia's Lazarevskoe Cemetery article gives 1956, ru.wikipedia's Smolensk Lutheran Cemetery article gives 1955, and en-Wikipedia's Euler article gives 1957 and ties the move to the 250th anniversary of the birth, which the two earlier readings do not support. 1956 is taken as the middle reading, not as a resolution
stops.campa: The remains and the monument are carried across the city to the Lazarevskoe cemetery of the Alexander Nevsky monastery, where the Academy's notable dead are gathered. The year is not settled: one article says 1956, the Russian article on the Lutheran ground says 1955, and the English article on Euler says 1957 and ties the move to the two hundred and fiftieth anniversary of the birth, which the earlier readings will not carry. The Soviet Union issues a stamp for that anniversary in 1957.

stops.name: University of Potsdam, the Euler Lecture
stops.date_confidence: the lecture is described only as annual and ongoing; the year is a placement and is not attested
stops.campa: Potsdam, where his fountains failed, holds an annual Euler Lecture. The Euler Society meets in America. The Euler Archive at the University of the Pacific digitises and translates the whole output and runs a journal for it. A crater on the Moon carries the name, and a minor planet, and a medal for combinatorics, and a book prize, and a gold medal, and a programming language derived from Algol, and a street in the eighth arrondissement of Paris, and an early French navy submarine.

stops.name: Charlottenburg, the hollow Earth he never proposed
stops.date_confidence: dated to Edward Sandifer's April 2007 column for the Mathematical Association of America, which is the refutation of record; the column itself could not be opened this session
stops.campa: In the hollow-earth literature Euler is the man who proposed a shell world with a sun a thousand kilometres wide at its centre, warming an inner civilisation. He proposed nothing of the kind. What he wrote, in the Letters, was a thought experiment about an object dropped down a hole drilled to the centre of the Earth. Edward Sandifer set the record straight in 2007. Symmes and Kircher belong to that lineage by their own choice; Euler was conscripted into it after his death, and stays conscripted.
suggested_refs: Edward Sandifer, 'Euler and the Hollow Earth: Fact or Fiction?', Mathematical Association of America, April 2007
